claim: Section 70531 of Public Law 119-21 is titled 'Modifications to de minimis entry privilege for commercial shipments' and amends section 321 of the Tariff Act of 1930 (19 U.S.C. 1321).
evidence: SEC. 70531. MODIFICATIONS TO DE MINIMIS ENTRY PRIVILEGE FOR COMMERCIAL SHIPMENTS.

claim: The subsection (b) amendments in section 70531 take effect on July 1, 2027.
evidence: The amendments made by this subsection shall take effect on July 1, 2027.

claim: Section 70531(a) adds a new subsection (c) to section 321 effective 30 days after enactment, and section 70531(b)(2) repeals that subsection (c) as part of the July 1, 2027 amendments.
evidence: Subsection (c) of such section 321, as added by subsection (a) of this section, is repealed.

claim: Section 70531(b)(1) amends section 321(a)(2) by striking the text from 'of this Act, or' through 'subdivision (2); and' and inserting 'of this Act; and'.
evidence: striking "of this Act, or" and all that follows through "subdivision (2); and" and inserting "of this Act; and"

claim: Section 70531(a) set a civil penalty of up to $5,000 for the first violation and up to $10,000 for each subsequent violation for using the de minimis privilege for an article whose importation violates other customs law, effective 30 days after enactment.
evidence: a civil penalty of up to $5,000 for the first violation and up to $10,000 for each subsequent violation

claim: CBP states that the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, enacted July 4, 2025, terminated the de minimis exemption effective July 1, 2027.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (Federal Register)
evidence: the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which was enacted on July 4, 2025, terminated the de minimis exemption effective July 1, 2027.

claim: Executive Order 14388 provides that de minimis does not apply to covered shipments regardless of value, origin, mode or method of entry, for goods entered on or after 12:01 a.m. EST on February 24, 2026.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (Federal Register)
evidence: regardless of value, country of origin, mode of transportation, or method of entry

claim: CBP's interim final rule effective June 24, 2026 amends 19 CFR 10.151 to suspend the exemption for all modes other than the international postal network until CBP determines otherwise and announces it in the Federal Register.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (Federal Register)
evidence: This interim final rule is effective on June 24, 2026.

claim: CBP's postal interim final rule is effective July 24, 2026 and references legislation terminating the de minimis exemption effective July 1, 2027.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (Federal Register)
evidence: This interim final rule is effective on July 24, 2026 ... effective July 1, 2027

claim: CBP's 'Low-Value Shipments' proposed rule of October 8, 2026 would change informal entry filing for goods valued at $2,500 or less, add an electronic mail entry type, a carrier data element and bonding; comments are due December 7, 2026.
publisher: Office of the Federal Register / National Archives (Federal Register)
evidence: Comments on the rule must be received on or before December 7, 2026.
